I routed this to Dunlin-235B primarily on capability grounds. This is a well-specified algebra problem with a single correct answer, so the deciding factor is reasoning/math performance. Dunlin scores higher on the relevant benchmarks — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.9), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 56.2), and Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 83.2) — which suggests stronger quantitative reasoning.

The task preferences didn't really factor in: this query is neither distasteful content (Dunlin's specialty) nor a retrieval/extraction task, and in any case the documentation notes preferences are dissociated from output quality. So I leaned on the measured capability gap, which favors Dunlin for a math problem.

(For what it's worth, the answer works out to b = 51: setting a+6 = b−6 = 5c with a+b+c = 99 gives a = 45, b = 51, c = 3.)
